main.title: Khiva Melon Festival - A Celebration of Traditions and Sweet Flavors!
main.description: Welcome to the paradise of Khiva melons! The annual Melon Festival held in ancient Khiva is a unique event showcasing delicious melons, national culture and hospitality!

about.info1: The annual Melon Festival held in the courtyard of Ichan Kala in ancient Khiva is not just an exhibition of sweet melons, but also a vivid expression of national traditions, hospitality and agricultural culture refined over centuries.
about.info2: The festival expands year by year, uniting thousands of guests not only from various regions of Uzbekistan but also from abroad. Here, rare varieties of the most delicious melons are presented, and every guest gets the chance to taste their unique flavor. Additionally, the festival features various entertainment programs, folk games, concerts and bazaars based on national traditions.
about.info3: The Melon Festival is not just a festival but a unique opportunity to experience the hospitality of ancient Khiva, its rich culture and priceless agricultural heritage. Every year we strive to celebrate this festival on an even grander scale and invite you to this magnificent celebration!

section.melons_subtitle: Famous sweet melon varieties such as Gurvak, Obi Novvot, Kokcha, and Shakarpalak cultivated in ancient Khorezm
section.melons_badge: Selected National Heritage • Khorezm Melon Culture

info.title: About the Festival
info.desc1: "Melon Festival" is one of the most important agricultural events held annually in Uzbekistan. During the festival, the finest melon varieties grown across the country are showcased and awarded.
info.participants: Participants: 200+ farming households from all regions of Uzbekistan
info.prize: Prize Fund: Total value of 300+ million soums
info.desc2: The festival features melon tastings, masterclasses, a national food fair, and cultural programs. Guests will have the opportunity to explore Uzbekistan's rich melon-growing traditions.
info.history_desc: Melon cultivation in Uzbekistan dates back over 3000 years. Today, there are more than 160 melon varieties in the country, each with a unique taste, aroma, and appearance.
